questions.stem: A data science team is describing the relationship between several technical terms to a new business stakeholder. Which statement correctly describes how the concepts relate to one another?
options: Machine learning is a subset of artificial intelligence, deep learning is a subset of machine learning, and generative AI is built on deep learning models.
Deep learning is a broader field that contains both artificial intelligence and machine learning.
Generative AI and machine learning are entirely separate fields with no overlap.
Artificial intelligence is a subset of machine learning, which is a subset of deep learning.
questions.explanation: AI is the broadest field; ML is a subset of AI; deep learning is a subset of ML that uses multi-layer neural networks; generative AI is built on deep learning foundation models. The other options reverse or break this nesting relationship.
questions.anchor: Knowing the hierarchy helps you pick the right AWS service tier for a workload.

questions.stem: A retailer has historical sales records labeled with the actual revenue for each day and wants a model to predict future daily revenue. Which type of machine learning best fits this task?
questions.explanation: Labeled historical data with a known target (revenue) used to predict a value is supervised learning. Unsupervised learning works on unlabeled data to find structure, and reinforcement learning learns from reward signals through interaction rather than labeled examples.
questions.anchor: Forecasting demand is a classic supervised regression use case.

questions.stem: An application must classify uploaded support tickets the moment they arrive and return a category within a few hundred milliseconds so an agent can respond. Which inferencing type is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: Low-latency, immediate, per-request predictions describe real-time inference. Batch inference processes large datasets on a schedule, and asynchronous inference queues longer-running requests where immediate response is not required.
questions.anchor: Amazon SageMaker AI offers real-time endpoints for exactly this pattern.

questions.stem: A company needs to score 50 million records overnight to generate a churn-risk report. There is no need for an immediate response, and minimizing cost is the priority. Which inferencing approach fits best?
questions.explanation: Large volumes processed on a schedule with no latency requirement is the textbook case for batch inference, which is cost-efficient because resources spin up only for the job. Real-time and synchronous single-record inference keep endpoints running and cost more for this volume.
questions.anchor: SageMaker AI batch transform is built for offline scoring of large datasets.

questions.stem: A model consistently gives lower approval rates to one demographic group even when financial qualifications are equal. Which responsible AI concept does this most directly illustrate?
questions.explanation: Systematically unequal outcomes across groups for equivalent inputs is bias, which threatens fairness. Overfitting describes a model memorizing training data, while latency and tokenization are unrelated to demographic disparity.
questions.anchor: Amazon SageMaker Clarify can measure this kind of disparity.

questions.stem: A team is cataloging its data assets before starting an ML project. Which of the following are examples of unstructured data? (Select TWO)
options: A relational table of order IDs and totals
A time-series of hourly temperature readings in a database column
A spreadsheet of employee names and salaries
questions.explanation: Audio recordings and images are unstructured data because they do not fit a predefined row-and-column schema. Relational tables, database time-series columns, and spreadsheets are structured (or semi-structured tabular) data.
questions.anchor: Most generative AI value comes from unlocking unstructured data.

questions.stem: Which description best defines an algorithm in a machine learning context?
options: The procedure or set of rules used to learn patterns from data and produce a model
The trained artifact that produces predictions on new inputs
The labeled examples used during training
The hardware accelerator used to speed up training
questions.explanation: An algorithm is the learning procedure applied to data; the model is the resulting trained artifact that makes predictions. The other options describe the model, the training data, and compute hardware respectively.
questions.anchor: Distinguishing algorithm from model clarifies what you are choosing versus producing.

questions.stem: A company deploys software that can perceive its environment, plan multi-step actions, call external tools, and pursue a goal with limited human intervention. Which term best describes this system?
questions.explanation: Goal-directed systems that plan, use tools, and act autonomously across multiple steps are agentic AI. A single classifier or clustering model performs one narrow task, and a static rules engine cannot plan or adapt.
questions.anchor: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore supports building agentic workflows.

questions.stem: A finance team needs to compute monthly interest using a fixed formula where every input always produces one exact, legally required output. Should they use machine learning?
options: No, a deterministic rules-based calculation is more appropriate than ML
Yes, train a regression model to approximate the interest
Yes, use a neural network for higher accuracy
Yes, use clustering to group the accounts first
questions.explanation: When the outcome is fully deterministic and a known formula gives the exact required answer, ML adds cost, risk, and approximation error for no benefit. ML suits problems with patterns too complex to hand-code, not exact arithmetic.
questions.anchor: Recognizing when NOT to use ML is an explicit exam objective.

questions.stem: A company wants to automatically convert recorded customer service calls into written text for analysis. Which AWS managed AI service is the best fit?
questions.explanation: Amazon Transcribe converts speech audio to text. Amazon Polly does the reverse (text to speech), Amazon Translate handles language translation, and Amazon Lex builds conversational chatbots.
questions.anchor: Speech-to-text is the first step in many call-center analytics pipelines.

questions.stem: A developer wants to add natural-language text capabilities such as sentiment analysis, entity recognition, and key-phrase extraction without training a model. Which AWS service should they choose?
questions.explanation: Amazon Comprehend is the managed NLP service for sentiment, entities, and key phrases. Polly is text-to-speech, Transcribe is speech-to-text, and Rekognition analyzes images and video.
questions.anchor: Comprehend lets teams extract insight from text without ML expertise.

questions.stem: A bank wants to flag potentially fraudulent transactions as legitimate or fraudulent based on labeled historical examples. Which ML technique is most appropriate?
options: Linear regression for a continuous value
questions.explanation: Assigning each transaction to one of two known categories (fraud or legitimate) is a classification task. Clustering finds groups in unlabeled data, and regression predicts continuous numeric values rather than categories.
questions.anchor: Fraud detection is a canonical binary classification problem.

questions.stem: A marketing analyst has a large set of customers with no labels and wants to discover natural segments for targeted campaigns. Which technique fits?
questions.explanation: Discovering natural groupings in unlabeled data is clustering, an unsupervised technique. Classification and regression require labeled targets, and reinforcement learning optimizes actions against a reward signal.
questions.anchor: Customer segmentation is the textbook clustering use case.

questions.stem: A company is evaluating where AI and ML can add real business value. In which of the following situations is using ML clearly appropriate? (Select TWO)
options: Detecting anomalies in millions of streaming sensor readings where patterns are too complex to hand-code
Recommending products based on patterns in past purchase behavior
Calculating sales tax from a fixed published rate table
Returning a stored record by exact primary key lookup
questions.explanation: Complex anomaly detection and pattern-based recommendations involve patterns too intricate to hand-code, where ML excels. Tax calculation from a fixed table, exact key lookups, and sequential numbering are deterministic operations better handled by conventional code.
questions.anchor: Match the tool to the problem: ML for patterns, code for determinism.

questions.stem: How does a foundation model differ from a traditional task-specific ML model?
options: A foundation model is pre-trained on broad data and can be adapted to many downstream tasks, while a traditional ML model is typically trained for one specific task
A foundation model can only perform a single classification task
A traditional ML model is always larger than a foundation model
Foundation models cannot be customized after pre-training
questions.explanation: Foundation models are pre-trained on large, broad datasets and adapted to many tasks via prompting, fine-tuning, or RAG, unlike traditional models built for one narrow task. Foundation models are generally larger and can be customized further.
questions.anchor: Amazon Bedrock provides access to multiple foundation models through one API.

questions.stem: A team wants to use leading foundation models through a fully managed, serverless API without provisioning infrastructure. Which AWS service is designed for this?
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock provides serverless, managed access to multiple foundation models through a single API. Self-hosting on EC2 requires managing infrastructure, Comprehend is task-specific NLP, and Lambda alone does not host foundation models.
questions.anchor: Bedrock is the default starting point for managed GenAI on AWS.

questions.stem: A binary classifier for a rare disease labels almost everyone as healthy and still reports 98% accuracy because the disease is rare. Which metric would best reveal that it misses most actual sick patients?
questions.explanation: Recall measures the proportion of actual positives the model correctly identifies, exposing missed sick patients that high accuracy hides on imbalanced data. Accuracy is misleading here, and latency and throughput are performance metrics, not quality metrics.
questions.anchor: On rare-event problems, recall and precision matter more than raw accuracy.

questions.stem: Which metric combines precision and recall into a single balanced score?
questions.explanation: The F1 score is the harmonic mean of precision and recall, giving one balanced number useful for imbalanced classes. Accuracy ignores class balance, while mean absolute error and R-squared are regression metrics.
questions.anchor: F1 is the go-to single metric when both false positives and false negatives matter.

questions.stem: A company wants an AI-powered assistant that answers employee questions using internal documents, with minimal custom development. Which AWS service is purpose-built for this?
questions.explanation: Amazon Q is a managed generative AI assistant that can answer questions grounded in enterprise data with minimal development. SageMaker AI training jobs build custom models, Polly is text-to-speech, and Macie discovers sensitive data.
questions.anchor: Amazon Q targets out-of-the-box enterprise assistant use cases.

questions.stem: A team is mapping the stages of a typical ML pipeline. Which of the following are legitimate stages in the ML lifecycle? (Select THREE)
questions.explanation: Data preparation, model training, and deployment with monitoring are core ML pipeline stages. Network provider selection and logo color are unrelated business or IT decisions, not ML lifecycle steps.
questions.anchor: MLOps automates and monitors these stages end to end.

questions.stem: What does MLOps primarily aim to achieve?
options: Reliable, repeatable processes for building, deploying, monitoring, and maintaining ML models in production
Replacing all data scientists with automated tools
Eliminating the need for any model evaluation
Storing models on local laptops for portability
questions.explanation: MLOps applies DevOps-style automation and governance to the full ML lifecycle for reliable, repeatable production operations. It complements rather than replaces practitioners and increases, not eliminates, evaluation and monitoring.
questions.anchor: MLOps is what keeps models healthy after the demo ends.

questions.stem: In generative AI, what is a token?
options: A unit of text such as a word or sub-word that the model processes
An access credential used to call the model API
questions.explanation: Tokens are the chunks of text (words or sub-words) that language models read and generate, and they are the basis of usage pricing. The other options confuse tokens with API keys, database indexes, or hardware memory.
questions.anchor: Token counts drive both context limits and cost on services like Amazon Bedrock.

questions.stem: A developer converts product descriptions into numeric vectors so similar items sit close together in vector space for semantic search. What are these numeric representations called?
questions.explanation: Embeddings are dense numeric vectors that capture semantic meaning so similar items are near each other in vector space. Tokens are text units, hyperparameters configure training, and checkpoints are saved model states.
questions.anchor: Embeddings power semantic search and RAG retrieval.

questions.stem: Why is large documentation often split into smaller chunks before being embedded for a retrieval system?
options: To create focused, appropriately sized passages that retrieve and fit within model context more effectively
To permanently delete the original document
To convert the text into a different spoken language
To increase the model's training data size
questions.explanation: Chunking breaks long documents into focused passages that embed well and fit within context limits, improving retrieval relevance. It does not delete originals, translate text, or expand training data.
questions.anchor: Good chunking strategy is central to high-quality RAG.

questions.stem: Which neural network architecture underlies modern large language models?
questions.explanation: Modern LLMs are built on the transformer architecture, which uses attention mechanisms to model relationships across a sequence. Decision trees, k-means, and linear regression are classical methods, not the basis of LLMs.
questions.anchor: The transformer is why long-range context understanding became practical.

questions.stem: An order of the foundation model lifecycle is being reviewed. Which sequence is correct?
options: Data selection, model selection, pre-training, fine-tuning, evaluation, deployment, feedback
Deployment, feedback, pre-training, data selection, evaluation
Evaluation, deployment, data selection, model selection, pre-training
Fine-tuning, data selection, deployment, pre-training, evaluation
questions.explanation: The lifecycle flows from selecting data and a model, through pre-training and fine-tuning, to evaluation, deployment, and ongoing feedback. The other orderings place deployment or evaluation before the model even exists.
questions.anchor: Feedback loops back into data selection for the next iteration.

questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of the Model Context Protocol (MCP) in agentic AI systems?
options: To provide a standardized way for AI agents and models to connect to external tools and data sources
To compress model weights for faster inference
To encrypt model checkpoints at rest
questions.explanation: MCP is an open standard that lets agents and models connect to external systems, tools, and data in a consistent way. It is not a compression, encryption, or speech transcription mechanism.
questions.anchor: MCP reduces custom glue code when wiring agents to enterprise systems.

questions.stem: A team is designing an AI agent that can complete multi-step business tasks. Which capabilities are characteristic of agentic AI systems? (Select THREE)
options: Calling external tools or APIs to take actions
Maintaining memory across steps of a task
Orchestrating a sequence of sub-tasks toward a goal
Guaranteeing a single deterministic output for every input
Eliminating the need for any foundation model
questions.explanation: Agentic systems use tools, retain memory, and orchestrate multi-step plans toward goals. They are nondeterministic by nature and still rely on an underlying foundation model to reason.
questions.anchor: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore provides building blocks for these capabilities.

questions.stem: A company is generating product photos from text descriptions. Which type of generative model is typically used to produce high-quality images?
questions.explanation: Diffusion models generate images by iteratively denoising random noise into a coherent picture and are the basis of leading text-to-image systems. The other options are classical ML methods not used for image generation.
questions.anchor: Image generation FMs on Amazon Bedrock use diffusion-style approaches.

questions.stem: A generative AI chatbot confidently states a refund policy that does not actually exist in any company document. What is this failure mode called?
questions.explanation: A model producing fluent but fabricated or unsupported information is a hallucination, a key disadvantage of generative AI. Overfitting and data drift are training and monitoring concerns, and latency is a performance issue.
questions.anchor: Grounding with RAG is a common way to reduce hallucinations.

questions.stem: A risk committee asks for the main disadvantages of generative AI they should plan for. Which of the following are genuine disadvantages? (Select THREE)
options: Potential for hallucinations and inaccurate outputs
Limited interpretability of how outputs are produced
Nondeterministic responses that can vary between runs
Inability to generate any natural language text
questions.explanation: Hallucinations, low interpretability, and nondeterminism are well-known disadvantages of generative AI. Generating natural language is a strength, not a limitation, and these models are not immune to bias.
questions.anchor: Governance plans must account for these inherent limitations.

questions.stem: A startup needs a chatbot that can hold flexible, conversational interactions and generate varied content on demand. Which advantage of generative AI most directly supports this need?
questions.explanation: Generative AI excels at adaptable, conversational, on-demand content generation, which is exactly the strength the chatbot needs. Determinism, zero cost, and legal indemnification are not characteristics of generative models.
questions.anchor: Conversational flexibility is the headline benefit of GenAI assistants.

questions.stem: An architect is choosing a foundation model for a latency-sensitive, cost-conscious customer-facing feature. Which factors should weigh into the model selection? (Select THREE)
options: Model capabilities for the required task
The color scheme of the company website
questions.explanation: Latency, cost, and task capability are core model-selection criteria, especially for a latency-sensitive, cost-conscious feature. Website color and personal brand preference are not legitimate technical selection factors.
questions.anchor: Model selection is always a balance of performance, cost, and constraints.

questions.stem: A product team wants to measure whether a new generative AI feature improves business outcomes. Which of the following is a business value metric rather than a model-quality metric?
options: Conversion rate of users who interact with the feature
questions.explanation: Conversion rate ties the feature to business value and revenue, unlike BLEU, F1, and perplexity, which are technical model-quality measures. Aligning to business metrics shows real return on the investment.
questions.anchor: Tie GenAI projects to ROI, conversion, ARPU, or CLV to justify them.

questions.stem: Why is interpretability often listed as a disadvantage of large generative models?
options: It can be difficult to explain exactly why the model produced a specific output
The models cannot produce any output at all
The models always reveal their full reasoning by default
Interpretability makes models slower to deploy on AWS
questions.explanation: Large models are often opaque, making it hard to explain why a particular output was generated, which complicates trust and auditing. They do produce output, do not automatically reveal reasoning, and interpretability is a transparency concern, not a deployment-speed issue.
questions.anchor: Low interpretability is why explainability tooling matters in regulated settings.

questions.stem: A team wants to browse, evaluate, and deploy pre-built foundation models and ML solutions to get started quickly within SageMaker. Which capability is designed for this?
questions.explanation: SageMaker JumpStart offers pre-built models and solution templates for quick deployment and experimentation. Macie discovers sensitive data, CloudTrail logs API activity, and Polly is text-to-speech.
questions.anchor: JumpStart shortens the path from idea to a running model.

questions.stem: An application has steady, high-volume traffic and needs guaranteed model throughput with predictable performance on Amazon Bedrock. Which pricing or capacity option fits best?
options: A free tier with no limits
questions.explanation: Provisioned throughput reserves dedicated model capacity for consistent, high-volume workloads with predictable performance. On-demand suits variable or low traffic, spot instances are not how Bedrock model capacity is purchased, and there is no unlimited free tier.
questions.anchor: Provisioned throughput trades commitment for guaranteed capacity.

questions.stem: A CISO asks why using a managed AWS generative AI service like Amazon Bedrock can be advantageous over building everything in-house. Which are valid advantages? (Select TWO)
options: Built-in security and compliance capabilities managed by AWS
Access to multiple foundation models through a unified API without managing infrastructure
A guarantee that the model will never produce an incorrect answer
Automatic removal of the need to evaluate outputs
questions.explanation: Managed services provide integrated security and compliance plus unified, infrastructure-free access to multiple models. They do not guarantee perfect answers, remove usage costs, or eliminate the need for evaluation.
questions.anchor: The managed model lets teams focus on the application, not the plumbing.

questions.stem: A developer needs to build, train, and host custom ML models with full control over the pipeline, including notebooks, training jobs, and endpoints. Which AWS service is the best fit?
questions.explanation: Amazon SageMaker AI is the end-to-end platform for building, training, and deploying custom ML models with full pipeline control. Amazon Q is a ready-made assistant, while Comprehend and Lex are narrow, pre-built AI services.
questions.anchor: SageMaker AI is the choice when you need to build, not just consume.

questions.stem: A company wants to deploy and operate AI agents securely at scale with managed infrastructure for memory, tools, and orchestration. Which AWS offering targets this need?
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore provides managed infrastructure for building and running AI agents at scale, including memory, tools, and orchestration. Polly is text-to-speech, Artifact provides compliance reports, and Macie discovers sensitive data.
questions.anchor: AgentCore handles the operational heavy lifting for agentic apps.

questions.stem: A global team needs a foundation model available in a specific AWS Region for data residency reasons. Which cost or deployment consideration does this primarily affect?
options: The number of tokens in the prompt
The choice of programming language for the SDK
questions.explanation: Data residency requirements depend on whether a given model is available in the required Region, a real coverage consideration. Temperature, token count, and SDK language do not address where data and inference are located.
questions.anchor: Always confirm model and Region availability before committing to a design.

questions.stem: A support team wants a chatbot to answer questions using the company's constantly changing internal knowledge base, with accurate citations and without retraining the model. Which approach best fits?
options: Full pre-training of a new foundation model
Increasing the maximum output length only
questions.explanation: RAG retrieves current, relevant documents at query time and grounds the model's answer in them, ideal for changing knowledge without retraining. Pre-training is far too costly, and adjusting temperature or output length does not add knowledge.
questions.anchor: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases provide managed RAG.

questions.stem: A developer increases the temperature parameter on a foundation model. What is the most likely effect on the output?
options: Responses become more random and creative
The model runs on faster hardware
The context window doubles in size
questions.explanation: Higher temperature increases randomness and creativity in token selection, while lower temperature makes output more focused and deterministic. Temperature does not change hardware or context window size.
questions.anchor: Lower temperature for factual tasks; raise it for brainstorming.

questions.stem: A team building a RAG application on AWS needs to store and query vector embeddings. Which of the following can serve as a vector store? (Select THREE)
questions.explanation: Amazon OpenSearch Service, Amazon Aurora, and Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL (with pgvector) can store and query vector embeddings for RAG. Polly and Transcribe are speech services and cannot serve as vector stores.
questions.anchor: Amazon Neptune also supports vector search for graph-based use cases.

questions.stem: A company wants to improve answers by including a few examples directly in the prompt at query time, without changing the model's weights. Which customization approach is this?
questions.explanation: Providing examples or context directly in the prompt without updating weights is in-context learning, the lowest-cost customization option. Fine-tuning, continuous pre-training, and distillation all modify or create model weights and cost more.
questions.anchor: Start with prompting and RAG before paying to fine-tune.

questions.stem: Among these FM customization options, which is generally the MOST expensive and resource-intensive to perform?
options: Pre-training a foundation model from scratch
Using RAG with an existing model
questions.explanation: Pre-training a foundation model from scratch requires massive data and compute, making it the most expensive option. RAG, in-context learning, and parameter tuning are far cheaper ways to adapt model behavior.
questions.anchor: Cost ladder: prompting and RAG, then fine-tuning, then pre-training.

questions.stem: A team has an application that repeatedly sends the same long system instructions before each user query and wants to reduce cost and latency. Which feature directly helps?
questions.explanation: Prompt caching reuses previously processed, repeated prompt content to lower cost and latency on subsequent calls. Temperature changes randomness, clustering is unrelated, and the context window cannot be disabled.
questions.anchor: Caching repeated context is a practical cost lever for production prompts.

questions.stem: A prompt instructs the model to 'think through the steps one at a time before giving the final answer' to improve reasoning on a math word problem. Which prompt engineering technique is this?
questions.explanation: Asking the model to reason step by step before answering is chain-of-thought prompting, which improves multi-step reasoning. Zero-shot gives no examples or steps, negative prompting specifies what to avoid, and prompt injection is an attack.
questions.anchor: Chain-of-thought is a simple, powerful technique for reasoning tasks.

questions.stem: A prompt includes three worked examples of the desired input-output format before posing the real question. Which technique does this describe?
questions.explanation: Providing several examples in the prompt to guide the response is few-shot prompting. Zero-shot includes no examples, while continuous pre-training and distillation are training techniques, not prompting styles.
questions.anchor: Few-shot examples steer format and tone without any training.

questions.stem: An attacker submits input designed to override the system instructions and make a chatbot ignore its safety rules and reveal restricted content. What is this attack called?
questions.explanation: Crafting input to override instructions and subvert intended behavior is prompt injection, a key generative AI security risk. Few-shot prompting and chain-of-thought are legitimate techniques, and embedding normalization is unrelated.
questions.anchor: Input validation and guardrails help mitigate prompt injection.

questions.stem: A team wants to store, version, and reuse standardized prompts across applications on AWS. Which capability supports this?
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock Prompt Management lets teams create, version, and reuse prompts consistently. Macie discovers sensitive data, CloudTrail logs API activity, and Polly is text-to-speech.
questions.anchor: Versioned prompts bring software discipline to prompt engineering.

questions.stem: A prompt engineer is documenting the constructs that make up an effective prompt. Which of the following are legitimate prompt engineering constructs? (Select THREE)
options: Clear instructions describing the desired output
Negative prompts specifying what to avoid
questions.explanation: Context, instructions, and negative prompts are real building blocks of a well-engineered prompt. A GPU serial number and a data center address have nothing to do with prompt construction.
questions.anchor: Strong prompts combine context, clear instructions, and constraints.

questions.stem: A team discovers that malicious documents added to a model's training or knowledge source caused it to learn harmful or false associations. Which risk does this describe?
questions.explanation: Injecting malicious or corrupt data into training or knowledge sources to corrupt model behavior is data poisoning. Prompt caching and provisioned throughput are performance features, and few-shot prompting is a benign technique.
questions.anchor: Data governance and source validation defend against poisoning.

questions.stem: A company adapts a general foundation model to legal terminology by further training it on a curated corpus of legal documents. Which fine-tuning approach is this?
questions.explanation: Further training a model on domain-specific data to specialize it is domain adaptation fine-tuning. Prompt caching and provisioned throughput are runtime features, and zero-shot prompting adds no training.
questions.anchor: Domain adaptation boosts performance on specialized vocabularies.

questions.stem: A team trains a large model's behavior to better match human preferences by using human ratings of model outputs as a reward signal. Which technique is this?
questions.explanation: Using human ratings as a reward signal to align model behavior is RLHF. Clustering and regression are unrelated classical methods, and batch inference is a deployment pattern, not a training alignment technique.
questions.anchor: RLHF is a major reason modern assistants follow instructions well.

questions.stem: A team wants a smaller, cheaper model that mimics the behavior of a large, expensive model. Which technique transfers the larger model's knowledge into the smaller one?
questions.explanation: Model distillation trains a smaller student model to reproduce a larger teacher model's behavior, cutting cost and latency. Pre-training from scratch is the opposite of leveraging an existing model, and temperature and prompt versioning do not shrink models.
questions.anchor: Distillation is a cost lever once a strong large model exists.

questions.stem: A team is preparing data to fine-tune a foundation model responsibly. Which data preparation practices are important? (Select THREE)
options: Ensuring the dataset is representative of real use cases
Applying data governance and proper labeling
Maximizing dataset size regardless of quality or relevance
Removing all human review from the labeling process
questions.explanation: Curation, representativeness, and governed labeling produce reliable fine-tuning results. Blindly maximizing size without quality introduces noise and bias, and removing human review undermines label quality.
questions.anchor: Garbage in, garbage out applies doubly to fine-tuning data.

questions.stem: A company periodically continues training an existing foundation model on large amounts of new unlabeled domain text to keep its general knowledge current. Which technique is this?
questions.explanation: Extending the model's pre-training on additional unlabeled domain data is continuous pre-training. In-context learning happens at inference, prompt injection is an attack, and output filtering is a safety control.
questions.anchor: Continuous pre-training refreshes broad knowledge over time.

questions.stem: What does instruction tuning primarily improve in a foundation model?
options: The model's ability to follow natural-language instructions across tasks
The physical size of the GPU cluster required
The number of Regions the model is available in
The encryption strength of stored checkpoints
questions.explanation: Instruction tuning fine-tunes a model on instruction-response pairs so it better follows directions across many tasks. It does not change hardware needs, regional availability, or encryption.
questions.anchor: Instruction tuning is why base models become helpful assistants.

questions.stem: A team needs to evaluate the quality of machine-generated summaries against reference summaries by measuring overlap of words and phrases. Which metric is designed for this?
questions.explanation: ROUGE measures overlap between generated and reference text, making it standard for summarization evaluation. Classifier precision-recall and mean squared error apply to other tasks, and latency is a performance metric.
questions.anchor: ROUGE for summarization; BLEU is more common for translation.

questions.stem: A localization team wants to evaluate the quality of machine-translated sentences against human reference translations. Which metric is most commonly used?
questions.explanation: BLEU is the standard metric for machine translation quality, comparing n-gram overlap with reference translations. ROUGE is primarily for summarization, R-squared is a regression metric, and throughput is performance, not quality.
questions.anchor: BLEU and translation go together on the exam.

questions.stem: A team uses a strong foundation model to automatically score the quality of another model's responses against a rubric. What is this evaluation approach called?
questions.explanation: Using a capable model to grade another model's outputs against criteria is the LLM-as-a-judge approach, useful for scaling subjective evaluation. BLEU is an overlap metric, batch inference is a deployment pattern, and data poisoning is an attack.
questions.anchor: LLM-as-a-judge scales evaluation where human review is too slow.

questions.stem: A regulated company wants people to review and approve high-risk AI outputs before they reach customers. Which evaluation or oversight approach does this describe?
options: Fully automated deployment with no review
questions.explanation: Inserting human review and approval into the workflow is human-in-the-loop, appropriate for high-risk outputs. Fully automated deployment removes oversight, and temperature and caching do not provide human review.
questions.anchor: Amazon Augmented AI (A2I) helps implement human review at scale.

questions.stem: A team wants a managed way to evaluate and compare foundation models on Amazon Bedrock using automatic metrics and human review. Which capability supports this?
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation provides managed automatic and human-based evaluation to compare models. Macie discovers sensitive data, Config tracks resource configuration, and Polly is text-to-speech.
questions.anchor: Bedrock Model Evaluation streamlines choosing the right model.

questions.stem: A product owner wants to align generative AI evaluation to business objectives rather than only technical scores. Which of the following are business-aligned evaluation measures? (Select TWO)
questions.explanation: Task completion rate and cost per interaction connect model performance to business outcomes. Attention heads, GPU clock speed, and parameter count are architectural or hardware details, not business measures.
questions.anchor: User satisfaction and cost per interaction tell the business story.

questions.stem: A company wants to block harmful content, filter sensitive topics, and redact personal information in its generative AI application on AWS. Which service is purpose-built for this?
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails enforces content filtering, denied topics, and sensitive-information redaction for generative AI apps. Polly is text-to-speech, CloudTrail logs API activity, and Translate handles language translation.
questions.anchor: Guardrails apply consistent safety policies across models.

questions.stem: A model performs almost perfectly on training data but poorly on new, unseen data. Which problem does this indicate?
questions.explanation: Strong training performance with weak generalization to new data is overfitting, often from high variance. Underfitting is the opposite (poor on both), and recall and latency are unrelated quality and performance measures.
questions.anchor: Overfitting is a variance problem; underfitting is a bias problem.

questions.stem: A team wants to detect bias in training data and in model predictions across demographic groups. Which AWS tool is designed for bias detection and explainability?
questions.explanation: Amazon SageMaker Clarify detects bias across groups and provides feature-importance explanations. Polly is text-to-speech, Artifact provides compliance documents, and Lex builds chatbots.
questions.anchor: Clarify covers both bias detection and explainability.

questions.stem: A governance lead is listing the core features of responsible AI. Which of the following are recognized responsible AI dimensions? (Select THREE)
questions.explanation: Fairness, safety, and veracity/robustness are core responsible AI dimensions, alongside inclusivity and transparency. Token throughput and storage cost are performance and cost concerns, not responsible AI principles.
questions.anchor: Responsible AI is about trust, not throughput.

questions.stem: A legal team is assessing risks specific to deploying generative AI. Which of the following are legitimate legal or ethical risks of generative AI? (Select TWO)
options: Intellectual property infringement in generated content
Biased outputs that disadvantage certain groups
Guaranteed elimination of all customer support staff
Automatic compliance with every global regulation
questions.explanation: IP infringement and biased outputs are real legal and ethical risks of generative AI. The remaining options are false promises; generative AI does not guarantee staffing outcomes, automatic compliance, or zero hallucinations.
questions.anchor: Legal review should cover IP, bias, and accuracy claims.

questions.stem: A team wants ongoing monitoring of a deployed model to catch data drift and quality degradation over time. Which AWS capability fits?
questions.explanation: Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor continuously watches deployed models for drift and quality issues. Polly, Artifact, and Translate serve speech, compliance documentation, and translation respectively.
questions.anchor: Monitoring catches the slow decay that evaluation at launch cannot.

questions.stem: A team wants a standardized document recording a model's intended use, training data, performance, and limitations to support transparency. Which AWS capability provides this?
questions.explanation: Amazon SageMaker Model Cards document a model's purpose, data, performance, and limitations for transparency and governance. Polly is text-to-speech, CloudTrail logs API activity, and Macie discovers sensitive data.
questions.anchor: Model cards are the standard transparency artifact for models.

questions.stem: Which of the following is generally considered the MOST interpretable, explainable model?
options: An ensemble of thousands of boosted trees
questions.explanation: A small decision tree exposes its decision path clearly, making it highly interpretable. Large neural networks, billion-parameter LLMs, and massive ensembles are far more opaque and harder to explain.
questions.anchor: Simpler models trade some accuracy for explainability.

questions.stem: A bank must explain to regulators why an individual loan application was declined by its model. Which responsible AI property is most important here?
questions.explanation: Regulators requiring a justification for individual decisions need explainability, the ability to articulate why an output occurred. Latency, throughput, and creativity do not satisfy a requirement to explain decisions.
questions.anchor: Explainability is non-negotiable in regulated lending.

questions.stem: A design team is building an explainable AI interface for non-technical users. Which human-centered design practice best supports trust and understanding?
options: Presenting clear, understandable explanations and allowing users to question or override decisions
Hiding all model reasoning to keep the interface simple
Showing raw model weights to every user
Removing any human ability to challenge an output
questions.explanation: Human-centered explainable AI gives users clear explanations and the ability to question or override decisions. Hiding reasoning, dumping raw weights, or blocking challenges all undermine trust and usability.
questions.anchor: Explainability is about the human's understanding, not raw internals.

questions.domainName: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.stem: A company wants to grant a SageMaker training job least-privilege access to a specific S3 bucket and nothing else. Which AWS mechanism should be used?
options: An IAM role with a scoped policy
Hardcoding access keys in the training script
questions.explanation: An IAM role with a narrowly scoped policy grants least-privilege access without embedding long-lived credentials. Hardcoding keys, making buckets public, and disabling logging all violate security best practices.
questions.anchor: Least privilege via IAM roles is foundational AWS security.

questions.domainName: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.stem: A team needs to discover and protect sensitive data such as personally identifiable information stored in Amazon S3 before using it for AI training. Which service is purpose-built for this?
questions.explanation: Amazon Macie uses machine learning to discover and classify sensitive data like PII in S3. Polly, Lex, and Translate provide speech, chatbot, and translation features, not data discovery.
questions.anchor: Find sensitive data with Macie before it reaches a training set.

questions.domainName: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.stem: A company wants to access Amazon Bedrock privately from its VPC without traffic traversing the public internet. Which AWS feature enables this?
options: An internet gateway with a public IP
questions.explanation: AWS PrivateLink provides private connectivity to services from within a VPC, keeping traffic off the public internet. An internet gateway exposes traffic publicly, and a public bucket or disabling encryption reduce security.
questions.anchor: PrivateLink keeps AI service traffic on the AWS private network.

questions.domainName: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.stem: Under the AWS shared responsibility model for a managed service like Amazon Bedrock, which responsibilities belong to the customer? (Select TWO)
options: Configuring IAM permissions and access controls for their applications
Managing how their data and prompts are handled and protected in their solution
Patching the physical servers in AWS data centers
Securing the underlying hypervisor of the managed service
Maintaining the global AWS network backbone
questions.explanation: Customers are responsible for IAM configuration and how they handle their own data and prompts (security in the cloud). AWS handles physical servers, hypervisors, and the network backbone (security of the cloud).
questions.anchor: Customer owns configuration and data; AWS owns the infrastructure.

questions.domainName: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.stem: A team wants to reduce hallucinations and ensure a generative AI assistant answers strictly from approved company documents with traceable sources. Which approach best achieves grounding?
options: Retrieval Augmented Generation with source citation
Raising the temperature to encourage creativity
questions.explanation: RAG grounds responses in approved documents and can cite sources, reducing hallucinations and improving traceability. Raising temperature increases randomness, and disabling logging or removing the knowledge base worsens reliability.
questions.anchor: Grounding plus citations is the standard anti-hallucination pattern.

questions.domainName: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.stem: A security review requires that all data used by an AI application be protected both while stored and while moving over the network. Which controls address this?
options: Encryption at rest and encryption in transit
questions.explanation: Protecting stored data requires encryption at rest, and protecting data on the network requires encryption in transit; both are needed. Doing only one leaves a gap, and relying on obscurity is not a security control.
questions.anchor: Encrypt data both at rest and in transit by default.

questions.domainName: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.stem: An auditor needs a complete record of who made which API calls in the AWS account, including calls to AI services, for accountability. Which service provides this?
questions.explanation: AWS CloudTrail records account API activity for audit and accountability. Polly, Comprehend, and Lex are AI services that perform speech, NLP, and chatbot tasks, not audit logging.
questions.anchor: CloudTrail is the audit trail for everything in the account.

questions.domainName: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.stem: A compliance team needs to download AWS audit reports and certifications such as SOC and ISO documents on demand. Which service provides these?
questions.explanation: AWS Artifact is the self-service portal for AWS compliance reports and certifications. CloudTrail logs API activity, Macie discovers sensitive data, and Polly is text-to-speech.
questions.anchor: Artifact is where auditors pull AWS compliance evidence.

questions.domainName: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.stem: A governance team wants to continuously assess whether AWS resource configurations comply with internal policies and flag drift. Which service fits?
questions.explanation: AWS Config continuously records and evaluates resource configurations against rules to detect noncompliance and drift. Polly, Translate, and Transcribe are speech and language services, not configuration governance tools.
questions.anchor: Config answers 'are my resources still compliant right now?'

questions.domainName: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.stem: A security team wants automated, continuous vulnerability scanning of their Amazon EC2 instances and container images supporting an AI workload. Which service is designed for this?
questions.explanation: Amazon Inspector performs automated, continuous vulnerability assessments of compute resources such as EC2 and container images. Artifact provides compliance documents, while Polly and Lex are AI services.
questions.anchor: Inspector finds known vulnerabilities before attackers do.

questions.domainName: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.stem: A data governance plan for an AI program is being drafted. Which of the following are legitimate data governance concerns? (Select THREE)
options: Logging and audit of data access
The brand of laptop used by data scientists
The font used in internal emails
questions.explanation: Retention and lifecycle, residency, and access logging are core data governance concerns. Laptop brand and email fonts are irrelevant to governing data.
questions.anchor: Governance covers where data lives, how long, and who touched it.

questions.domainName: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.stem: An organization wants a structured framework to classify the security scope and responsibilities of different generative AI deployment patterns, from consumer apps to self-trained models. Which resource is intended for this?
options: The Generative AI Security Scoping Matrix
The Amazon S3 storage class guide
questions.explanation: The Generative AI Security Scoping Matrix is a framework for classifying GenAI deployment scopes and their security responsibilities. The other options are product references unrelated to security scoping.
questions.anchor: The scoping matrix helps teams reason about shared responsibility for GenAI.

questions.domainName: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.stem: A team wants automated recommendations to optimize cost, performance, security, and fault tolerance across their AWS environment. Which service provides these checks?
questions.explanation: AWS Trusted Advisor inspects an account and recommends improvements across cost, performance, security, and fault tolerance. Polly, Transcribe, and Comprehend are AI services, not advisory tooling.
questions.anchor: Trusted Advisor is the account-wide best-practice checker.

questions.stem: A team is categorizing the learning paradigms behind several projects. Which of the following pairings of scenario to learning type are correct? (Select TWO)
options: Predicting house prices from labeled historical sales is supervised learning
Grouping unlabeled customers into segments is unsupervised learning
Predicting house prices from labeled sales is reinforcement learning
Grouping unlabeled customers is supervised learning
Translating text is always unsupervised clustering
questions.explanation: Labeled-target prediction is supervised learning, and grouping unlabeled data into segments is unsupervised learning. The remaining options misassign reinforcement learning to a labeled prediction task and mislabel clustering and translation.
questions.anchor: Match the data (labeled vs unlabeled) to the paradigm.

questions.stem: A CFO wants metrics that demonstrate the business value of a generative AI initiative. Which of the following are business value metrics? (Select THREE)
options: Number of transformer layers in the model
Size of the model checkpoint file in gigabytes
questions.explanation: ROI, ARPU, and CLV connect the initiative to financial outcomes. The number of transformer layers and checkpoint file size are technical attributes that do not measure business value.
questions.anchor: Speak to the CFO in ROI, ARPU, and CLV, not layer counts.

questions.stem: An architect is selecting a foundation model for a multilingual, low-latency mobile feature. Which selection criteria are directly relevant? (Select THREE)
options: Model size and its effect on cost and speed
The favorite color of the project sponsor
The number of letters in the model's name
questions.explanation: Multilingual support, latency, and model size all directly affect fit for a multilingual, low-latency feature. Sponsor color preference and name length are not selection criteria.
questions.anchor: FM selection weighs modality, latency, size, cost, and customization.

questions.stem: A team is choosing automatic metrics to evaluate generated text. Which of the following are recognized text-generation evaluation metrics? (Select THREE)
questions.explanation: ROUGE, BLEU, and BERTScore are established metrics for evaluating generated text quality. GPU temperature and disk IOPS are hardware and storage measurements, not quality metrics.
questions.anchor: BERTScore adds semantic similarity beyond simple n-gram overlap.

questions.domainName: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.stem: A security team is hardening a generative AI application against data leakage and abuse. Which of the following are appropriate controls? (Select THREE)
options: Output filtering to block sensitive or toxic content
Encryption of data in transit and at rest
Audit logging of prompts and responses
Embedding long-lived access keys in client-side code
Granting every user full administrator permissions
questions.explanation: Output filtering, encryption, and audit logging are sound controls against leakage and abuse. Embedding long-lived keys in client code and granting blanket admin rights are serious security anti-patterns.
questions.anchor: Defense in depth: filter outputs, encrypt data, and log access.
